title: Task Splitting
concept: Breaking long tasks into small pieces and yielding control periodically is essential for maintaining UI responsiveness.

steps.title: Defining a Blocking Task
steps.explanation:
The `heavy()` function defines a long task that completely blocks the main thread.
While it runs, the browser's UI freezes until all one billion iterations complete.
This is called 'UI freezing'.

steps.title: Defining Chunking: splitting the work
steps.explanation:
The `heavyChunk()` function is designed to break the long task into small pieces (Chunks).
Each call only does one million iterations, so the main thread isn't held for too long.
steps.keyInsight: The technique of breaking a huge task into pieces to reduce the time each execution takes.

steps.title: Defining Yielding: handing back control
steps.explanation:
After each chunk, `heavyChunk()` calls `setTimeout(heavyChunk, 0)` to send the next chunk to the Task Queue.
This intentionally empties the Call Stack, giving the browser a chance to handle rendering and user input (Yield).

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid API for yielding during long tasks?
quiz.explanation: A synchronous loop like `while(true)` never empties the main thread — it holds it indefinitely.

misconceptions.wrong: Breaking tasks with Promises prevents the screen from freezing
misconceptions.correct:
Not exactly.
Promises have higher priority than rendering.
misconceptions.why:
If Promises (microtasks) keep chaining, the browser never gets to the rendering step.
To yield to rendering, use setTimeout (macrotask) or a scheduler API.

keyTakeaway: Break huge tasks into small chunks and yield frequently.
